walk query.#comment: Shared step: OSM query around the location heli. Params QUERY and SIZE. Returns the data (param my_data of the call).

walk cleanup.#comment: Destroys every object created by buttons 5, 6 and 7. The test never goes above 12 objects.

walk cleanup.value: DONE: test objects removed (map points stay until the mission is restarted)

walk test arms.#comment: Button 5: from the heli position (the accident) take the closest road node that is a junction (more than one parent way, like road nodes generator), take its first parent way, and walk the way in both directions for 60 m and 400 m. The result is compared with the current extrapolation (point 60 m / 400 m behind the node on the straight line node -> accident).

DONE: markers placed, see the lines below (log: table R&E_osm_road_walk_arms)

walk test cars.#comment: Button 6, run after 5: four recognisable vehicles. A SERVICE VAN: created at F60 (F400 if reached) and pointed at the next node (point_object only). B GARBAGE TRUCK: created at B60 (B400), pointed at the node ahead and then driven to it (a drive from a bend may not straighten the vehicle, the pointing before the drive is needed). C FIAT: created at the junction node, pointed at F60, moved 2.5 m to the right and POINTED AGAIN after the move. D FIAT: same as C but 6 m to the right and NOT pointed again after the move (the old test: a move_object with heading 0 resets the heading, the baseline always points again after it). If the explanation is right, A, B and C follow the road and D is turned by a different angle.

walk test route tail.#comment: Button 7: stop slots from the route array. Route from a point 600 m away to the helicopter position (the accident), the end snaps to the nearest road. The route is walked backward from its last entry: slots at 15, 30 and 45 m along the route (fire, ambulance, police queue), aligned with the route.

else.value: FAILED: no route (duration null or 0): this is the router-failure fallback case

Only reads data, creates no object.

walk test power and straights.value: A straight run of 100 m or more is the criterion for the 30West powerline (6 or 7 poles in line); poles are not placed at random.

walk test pole series plain.#comment: Button 10: two series of the 30West powerline (one object = 9 poles in line) 245 m apart on a straight stretch of road, 8 m to its right, both pointed the same way along the line from A to B (the assets interlock head to tail, so they must not point at each other); mode 'plain'. Scans the major road ways within 1500 m, keeps the nearest straight run of at least 500 m (else the longest). If the title is not installed a green marker is created instead.

briefing.text: Park on the ground within 100-300 m of a road, ideally next to a bend or a side street: the helicopter position is the accident. Buttons 5, 6 and 7 create at most 12 objects; use 9 to remove them. Run 5 before 6.
